decisions.reason: It is a core extension of the firm’s airfield-lighting business, was given increasing prominence, and likely meets or exceeds aspiration levels well enough that slack should be used to continue scaling it.

As a strategically aligned surveillance interface with dedicated market presentation, it fits the firm’s integrated-airport direction and shows no sign of falling below aspirations strongly enough to justify withdrawal.

This training program complements the installed systems base, deepens customer relationships, and is worth retaining under uncertainty because its resource needs are modest relative to the firm’s available slack.

Although less prominently presented, the course supports the core airfield-lighting offer and there is too little evidence of serious underperformance to redeploy even these limited service resources elsewhere.

Collaboration software is central to the firm’s stated move toward real-time information sharing and coordinated airport operations, so management would keep it unless performance clearly missed aspirations, which is not indicated here.

The MLAT surveillance system is a high-fit, R&D-intensive adjacent product in a growing innovative market, and its strong launch positioning supports keeping it while the firm continues learning and commercialization.
